description:
Two different closures passed through a helper into a function where the closure is not the first parameter fail on all three paths. Predates the epic: same failure on the base binary at 6ac603ac5. The distiller hits it through Enum.max/min with a fallback (distill lines 278, 279, 286, 298), so it blocks the Enum ticket.

Smallest repro (scratchpad sc833/k.fz):

    defp ext(_x, f), do: f.()
    def pick(f), do: ext(0, f)
    def main() do
      dbg([pick(fn -> 0 end), pick(fn -> 1 end)])
    end

Expected on every path: [0, 1].

- interp: "backend dispatch call requires semantic argument 1 value 0: backend generic callable shape ShapeId(14) has no published lane"
- run: "backend value ValueId(1) ... must be runtime-materializable" (artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan: "native attempted to rematerialize generic callable shape ... first-class callable values must come from transport publication lanes")
- build: panic at jobs/native.rs:3944, value=Absent

Passing neighbours, which isolate the trigger:
- closure is ext's only parameter: works.
- closure is ext's FIRST parameter (ext(f, x)): works.
- the same closure value passed twice: works.
- ext called directly from main with two closures (no helper hop): works.
- pick called once: works.

Neighbor to check for a shared cause: fz-afu.14 (a helper-built closure chosen by a case loses its value; "backend value was absent").

Paper first: answer by hand which lane carries the closure into ext's argument 1, find the first difference, fix at the source. Proposal page before building.
title: Two different closures passed through a helper to a shared function fail to compile
